ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-02-15
Provider: Dr. Michael Rodriguez, MD
Department: Nephrology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fatigue and swelling around eyes and lower legs following recent strep throat

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is an 8-year-old male with relapsing steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome who returns to Nephrology one month after streptococcal pharyngitis. He is brought to the physician by his parents due to recent onset of fatigue and decreased energy levels. They report a sore throat 2 weeks ago treated with penicillin, and began noticing swelling around his eyes and lower legs 5 days ago.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Obstructive sleep apnea (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Minimal change disease (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Streptococcal pharyngitis (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome (Minimal Change Disease), relapsing type
- Recurrent acute otitis media
- Adenotonsillar hypertrophy

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tube placement at age 4

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 1 spray in each nostril daily
- Montelukast 4 mg chewable tablet nightly

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with obstructive sleep apnea
- Paternal cousin with childhood nephrotic syndrome
- Maternal grandmother with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: First-grade student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, heart rate is 80 beats/min, respiratory rate is 20 breaths/min, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals periorbital edema, pitting edema in the ankles, and pallor.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory findings show hemoglobin of 12 g/dL, serum cholesterol of 300 mg/dL, and urinalysis with 2-3 RBCs/hpf, negative glucose, and 3+ protein.

OTHER STUDIES:
A renal biopsy is performed to evaluate the cause.

He had a mild fever and sore throat about 10 days ago that resolved without medical attention. His mother noticed that his urine has become darker and appears “tea-colored.” He has been more fatigued than usual and refused to eat breakfast this morning.

- Paternal cousin with childhood nephrotic syndrome
- Maternal grandmother with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:

VITAL SIGNS:
On physical examination, his temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), heart rate is 92/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 120/74 mm Hg.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-03-15
Provider: Dr. David Park, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden-onset left flank pain and gross hematuria in patient with recent nephrotic syndrome flare

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is an 8-year-old male with a history of relapsing minimal change disease (initially diagnosed July 2020, with recent relapse February 2022 following streptococcal pharyngitis) and obstructive sleep apnea who presents with sudden-onset left flank pain and gross hematuria. He was diagnosed with minimal change disease three weeks ago after presenting with generalized edema and heavy proteinuria. He was started on oral prednisone and initially responded well, with some reduction in swelling. However, over the last two days, his parents report that he has seemed more fatigued and complained of vague abdominal discomfort. This morning, he developed sharp pain in his left flank and passed dark red urine. He denies dysuria, fever, or recent trauma.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Obstructive sleep apnea (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Minimal change disease (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Streptococcal pharyngitis (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome (Minimal Change Disease), relapsing type
- Recurrent acute otitis media
- Adenotonsillar hypertrophy

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 1 spray in each nostril daily
- Montelukast 4 mg chewable tablet nightly

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with obstructive sleep apnea
- Paternal cousin with childhood nephrotic syndrome
- Maternal grandmother with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: First-grade student.

VITAL SIGNS:
Temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 102/68 mmHg, and heart rate is 108/min

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
He appears mildly uncomfortable but is alert and cooperative. There is mild periorbital and pedal edema, and tenderness to palpation over the left costovertebral angle. The rest of the exam is unremarkable.
